question: Cloud kicks needs to ensure appropriate shipping details are used in orders. Reps should have a streamlined solutions to update the shipping address on selected orders associated with an account when the shipping address is changed on the account. How should the administrator deliver this requirement?
optionA: An autolaunched flow on the order page that updates all open orders shipping addresses whenever the account shipping addresses changes.
optionB: An autolaunched flow on the account page that updates all open orders shipping addresses whenever the account shipping addresses changes.
optionC: A screen flow on the order page that lets the reps choose the updated account shipping address in all open associatedorders
optionD: A screen flow on the account page that lets the reps choose the updated account shipping address in all open associated orders
explanation:
The word that decides this item is "selected". Reps are not updating every open order, they are choosing which ones to update, and a choice needs a screen.
So the answer is a screen flow, placed on the Account page - the record where the address actually changed. The flow can query the account's open orders, present them for selection, and write the new shipping address to the ones the rep picks.
An autolaunched flow has no user interface at all, so on either object it would update every matching order with no chance to exclude any. Putting the screen flow on the Order page is the wrong context: the rep would be on one order at a time, which is the opposite of updating a chosen set in one pass.

question: Ursa Major Solar has a path on Case. The Company wants to require its users to follow the status values as they are on the path. Agents should be prohibited from preventing the case back to a previous status. Which Feature Should an administrator use to fulfill this request?
explanation:
Path displays the stages and guides reps through them, but it does not enforce anything - a user can still set Status back to an earlier value, and Path will happily show them there. Enforcement is a validation rule.
The rule compares the new value against the old one. Because PRIORVALUE and ISCHANGED are available in validation formulas, a rule can detect that Status moved from a later step to an earlier one and block the save with an error.
The other options cannot refuse a save. A global value set standardises which values exist across fields but imposes no order. Predefined field values pre-populate a field on an action. Dependent picklists filter one picklist by another's value, which is about available choices, not about the direction of travel between them.

explanation:

question: Sales reps at NorthernTrail Outfitters have asked for a way to change the Probability field value of their Opportunities. What should an administrator suggest to meet this request?
optionA: Define a new Stage picklist value.
optionB: Create a custom field on Opportunity.
optionD: Make the field editable on page layouts
explanation:
Probability is a standard field on Opportunity that Salesforce populates from the stage - each stage value carries a default probability, and moving the stage overwrites the field.
It is not, however, read-only. Adding Probability to the page layout as an editable field lets reps type their own number over the stage-derived default. Note that a later stage change writes the default back, so a manual value survives only until the deal moves.
The other options miss the request. A new stage picklist value changes the process rather than making the existing field editable. A custom field would sit beside the standard one and be ignored by forecasting. Forecasting consumes the probability and forecast category; it does not control whether reps can edit the field.

question: An administrator at Cloud Kicks wants to deactivate a User who has left the company. What are two reasons that would prevent a user from being deactivated? Choose 2 answers
optionA: The use is part of a territory hierarchy.
optionB: The User is in a Custom hierarchy field.
optionC: The User is assigned in workflow email alert.
optionD: The User is the highest role in the role hierarchy
explanation:
Salesforce's considerations for deactivating users name both of these. A user selected in a custom hierarchy field cannot be deactivated — the save fails with "Cannot inactivate user that is the value of a hierarchy field" — and the block persists even if the field is deleted, until the field is permanently erased. A user who is the sole recipient of a workflow email alert is likewise blocked.
Territory assignment prevents nothing: deactivating a user removes them from their territories automatically. Being highest in the role hierarchy is no obstacle either — the role is simply left without an active user.

question: The events manager at dream house realty has a hot lead from a successful open house that needs to become a contact with an associated opportunity. How should this be accomplished from the campaign keeping the associated campaign member history?
optionA: Delete the lead and create a new contact and opportunity.

The alternatives all break that link. Deleting the lead destroys the campaign member record with it. Cloning creates a record with no campaign history behind it. Adding a contact to the campaign afterwards produces a fresh membership dated today, which is not the same as the history from the open house.

question: New Leads needs to be routed to the correct sales person based on the lead address. How should the administrator configure this requirement?
explanation:
Assignment rules are the routing mechanism. Set Up Assignment Rules describes them as conditions that determine how leads or cases are processed, assigning each to a specified user or queue.
For this requirement the rule entries test address fields - City, State/Province, Country, or postal code ranges - and send matching leads to the rep who owns that territory. Entries are evaluated in order, so the first match wins and a final catch-all entry can hold anything that fits no rule.
Nothing else here routes a record. A formula field derives a value for display; it assigns nothing. Escalation rules act on cases after time has passed, not on new leads. A validation rule can only block a save.

question: A Sales user is trying to manage Campaign Members for an upcoming networking event. The user can view the Campaign, but add new Campaign Members or update Member statuses. How can an administrator troubleshoot this problem?
optionA: Create a permission set to allow the user to edit Campaign Members.
optionB: Provide the user access to both Leads and Contacts to edit all Members.
optionC: Make sure the Marketing User Checkbox is checked on the user record page.
optionD: Run a Campaign report and update any Member information via Data Loader.
explanation:
Campaign management is gated by a checkbox on the user record rather than by object permissions alone. Who has access to Campaigns? sets out the split: depending on sharing, users can view campaigns, view the advanced campaign setup, or run campaign reports, but only designated marketing users get to create and manage them.
So a user who can see the campaign but cannot add members or change member statuses is almost always missing the Marketing User checkbox. Note that the checkbox works alongside ordinary permissions rather than replacing them - the user still needs read and edit access to campaigns and to the leads or contacts being added.
A permission set cannot substitute, because this is a user-record attribute rather than an object permission. Granting more access to leads and contacts does not unlock campaign member management. Updating records through Data Loader works around the symptom instead of fixing the access.

question: Sales and Customer Care at Ursa Major Solar need to see different fields on the Case related list from the Account record. Sales users want to see Case created date and status while Customer Care would like to see owner, status, and contact. What should the administrator use to achieve this?

Related list columns are a page layout property. In the page layout editor you open the Cases related list's properties and choose which fields appear as columns, in what order, and how the rows sort.
Because each layout carries its own version of that related list, assigning one layout to Sales and another to Customer Care gives each team its own column set on the same Account page - created date and status for one, owner, status and contact for the other.
The other editors do different jobs: compact layouts drive the highlights panel and mobile preview, search layouts control results and list columns for search, and lookup filters restrict which records a lookup field will accept.

question: An administrator at AW Computing has been asked to help the Support team with report folders. They want a folder called Support Reports and two folders underneath called Helpdesk and R&D. The Support organization uses public groups for Support Agents, R&D, and Managers. Support agents should be able to run Helpdesk reports, but should not be able to view R&D reports. Support managers should be able to view and edit all reports. Which two ways should these folders be shared? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Share the R&D folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.
optionB: Share the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents with View access.
optionC: Share the Support Reports folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.
optionD: hare the Support Reports folder with Support Agents with View Access.
explanation:
Report folder access is granted per folder, to public groups, roles or territories, at View, Edit or Manage level - and it does not cascade, since report folders in Lightning are a flat list rather than a true hierarchy. Each folder has to be shared on its own terms.
That is what makes these two the right pair. Sharing the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents at View access lets them run those reports without touching R&D. Sharing the Support Reports folder with Support Managers at Edit access gives managers the run-and-modify rights they were asked for.
The two rejected options both misfire on the agents' restriction. Sharing the parent Support Reports folder with Support Agents would be an attempt to grant access by containment, and sharing R&D with managers at Edit is already covered without addressing what agents may see.

question: Cloud Kicks has decided to delete a custom field. What will happen to the data in the field when it is deleted?
optionA: The data in the field is stored for 15 days.
optionC: The data associated with the field is required.
optionD: The data is restorable from the recycle bin.
explanation:
Deleting a custom field does not destroy its data straight away. The field and its contents move to the Deleted Fields list for that object and stay there for 15 days. During that window you can undelete the field, and its data returns with it, or erase it to hard-delete immediately. After 15 days Salesforce purges it permanently.
Two details worth holding on to: the field keeps counting against the object's custom field limit until it is purged, and it is the Deleted Fields list in Object Manager that holds it — not the record Recycle Bin.

question: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has created an approval process for time off requests. Which two automated actions areavailable to be added as part of the approval process? Choose 2 answers
explanation:
Classic approval processes accept automated actions at four points - initial submission, each approval step, final approval or rejection, and recall - and the actions available are the workflow action types: field updates, email alerts, tasks, and outbound messages.
Field Update and Email Alert are therefore both available, and both are the ones this scenario would use: stamp a status field as the time-off request advances, and mail the requester and the approver.
A Chatter post is not among the automated actions a classic approval process can attach. Neither is an autolaunched flow - to involve a flow you either move to Flow Approval Processes or have a record-triggered flow react to the field the approval process updated.
References:

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Administrator wants to trigger afollow-up task for the opportunity owner when they close an opportunity as won and another task after 60 days to check in with the customer. which two automation tools should the administrator use? Choose 2 answers
explanation:
Both halves of the requirement are "create a task", and the two things here that can do that on a schedule are Process Builder and Workflow Rules. A workflow rule creates the immediate task when the stage becomes Closed Won, and a time trigger — an offset of up to 999 days from a date field on the record — creates the 60-day check-in. Process Builder achieves the same with immediate and scheduled actions on one criteria node.
A Field Update is an action available inside those tools rather than a tool in its own right, and it can only overwrite a field; it cannot create a task. An Outbound Message sends data to an external endpoint.
Worth knowing in practice: Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 December 2025, and new automation of this shape is built with scheduled paths in Flow Builder.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.workflow_time_dependent.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: A Field Update cannot create a task, so it can never satisfy a requirement whose every step is "create a task" — and it is an action inside an automation tool, not a tool. Process Builder and Workflow Rules are the two options that can create both the immediate and the time-delayed task.

question: Brokers at DreamHouse Realty need to see certain information about one or more cases when referencing the contact record. This record case Name, Case ID, Customer Name, Case Reason, Case Status, and Case Creation Date. Which two changes in Setup should the administrator make?
optionA: Use the page layout editor to change the related list type to Enhanced List.
optionB: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Related List as the related list type.
optionC: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Enhanced List as the related list type.
optionD: Use the page layout editor to include the appropriate column in the Cases related list.
explanation:
Two settings are involved, in two different places. The columns themselves come from the page layout editor: edit the Cases related list there and add Case ID, Customer Name, Case Reason and the rest. But a standard related list in Lightning Experience renders only four columns, so the six requested fields will not all appear. Setting the Related List component's Related List Type to Enhanced List in the Lightning App Builder raises the limit to ten columns, and adds column resizing, sorting and text wrapping.
Leaving the type as the plain Related List keeps the four-column cap, and the related list type cannot be set from the page layout editor at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_create_dynamic_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

corrected.note: Six fields were requested, and a standard Lightning related list displays at most four columns; Enhanced List raises that to ten. The previously marked plain "Related List" type would silently drop two of the six fields.

question: AW Computing has six sales teams in a region. These teams always consists of the same account manager, engineer, and assistant. What should the administrator configure to make it easier for teams to collaborate with the same customer?
optionA: Enable and configure standard opportunity teams with splits.
optionB: Propose the users manually share all their accounts with their teammates.
optionC: Create a queue for each team and assign account ownership to the queue.
optionD: Enable account teams and show the users how to set up a default account team.
explanation:
Six teams with a fixed membership is the case account teams were designed for. Enable account teams, then have each user build a default account team of their account manager, engineer and assistant; that team is then added automatically to the accounts they own, with the access level and role each member should have.
The alternative of manual sharing puts the same work on people every time an account is created, and nothing keeps it consistent.
Opportunity teams with splits solve a different problem - crediting revenue across a deal - and would not give collaborative access to the account itself. Assigning account ownership to a queue is not possible for accounts, and a queue holds records for claiming rather than sharing them with a standing team.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.accountteam_def.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Sales director at Cloud Kicks wants to be able to predict upcoming revenue in the next several fiscal quarters so they can set goals and benchmark how reps are performing. Which two features should the administrator configure? Choose 2 answers
explanation:
Forecasting is the feature that projects revenue across future fiscal periods, which is what lets a sales director see what is expected to close in coming quarters and measure reps against it. Forecasting rests on Opportunity Stages: each stage carries a probability and maps to a forecast category, and that mapping is what turns an open pipeline into a revenue projection.
Sales Quotes are customer-facing pricing documents and project nothing (note that quotes are not the same thing as sales quotas). An Opportunity List View shows the records that exist today but makes no prediction about future quarters.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The marked answer left out Forecasting entirely, which is the one feature that actually predicts revenue by fiscal quarter. Its own explanation argues for Forecasting and Opportunity Stages and never mentions the two options it had marked correct.

question: The administrator at DreamHouse Realty added an email quick action to the Case page layout and is unable to see the action on the case feed. Which feature must be enabled to ensure the quick action will be displayed as expected?
explanation:
Send Email Action Considerations for Cases states the dependency in one line: "Turn on Email-to-Case to enable the case-specific Send Email action on cases." Until Email-to-Case is on, the action can sit on the layout and still not appear in the case feed.
That is why the other options do not help. Email templates supply the body of a message once the action exists. Email alerts are an automation action that sends mail without any user involvement. Email notifications are a user preference. None of them is the switch that turns the case Send Email action on.
Worth knowing for the exam and for real orgs: enabling Email-to-Case for this purpose does not oblige you to configure routing addresses - the considerations note that this requirement is separate from routing or org-wide addresses.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.case_interaction_send_email_quick_action_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.setting_up_email-to-case.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) is partnering with a used shoe store and second-hand bicycle emporium. CK has an automated business process it wants to run once a week to count the number of open cases related to an account. How should the administrator recommend automating this business process?
optionA: Create a workflow rule with an outbound message.
optionB: Set up a scheduled process in Process Builder.
optionC: Configure a scheduled flow in flow Builder.
optionD: Use a process to update the account when it is edited
explanation:
Flow Builder supports creating a scheduled flow that can run at specified intervals and perform actions on a set of records that meet certaincriteria.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_schedule.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Universal Containers is reviewing current security settings in the company's Salesforce org. What Should the administrator do to prevent unauthorized access to Salesforce?
optionD: Enable caching and autocomplete on login page
explanation:
Multi-factor authentication is the setting that actually raises the bar against unauthorized access: on top of the password, the user has to present a second factor - an authenticator app, a security key, or a built-in authenticator - so a stolen password alone is not enough. Salesforce turns it on org-wide from Identity Verification in Setup.
The other three options move security in the wrong direction or do not touch login at all. Disabling TLS requirements would expose sessions that are currently encrypted. Caching and autocomplete on the login page make it easier for the next person at that machine to sign in as the user. Organization-wide defaults govern which records a user can see once they are already inside, not whether the wrong person can get in.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_overview_2fa.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.security_mfa_org_wide_setting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which tool should an administrator use to review recent configuration changes made in their org?
explanation:
Setup Audit Trail is the record of configuration changes. It names the date, the user, and what was changed; the page shows the 20 most recent entries and the Download link exports the full history for the past 180 days, after which entries are deleted.
The distractors each track something else. Debug logs capture what happened during a single transaction - queries, workflow, Apex - not who changed a setting. Field History Tracking records changes to field values on records, which is data rather than configuration. Release Updates (the feature that replaced Critical Updates) announces changes Salesforce is making to the platform, not changes your administrators made.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.admin_monitorsetup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has a custom object named shoe. The administrator has been asked to ensure that when a relationship is created between Account and shoe to prevent orphaned shoe records. What should the administrator do to complete this requirement?
explanation:
An orphan is a child record with no parent, and master-detail is the relationship that makes that impossible. The relationship field on the detail record is required, so a Shoe cannot be saved without an Account, and it cannot later be left dangling - if the Account is deleted, its Shoes are deleted with it rather than surviving without a parent.
A plain lookup would allow exactly what the requirement forbids: the field is optional, and deleting the account clears it and leaves the Shoe behind.
Of the other options, an encrypted lookup does not exist. An indirect lookup is a real relationship type but belongs to external objects, linking them to a standard or custom object by an external id. A hierarchical relationship is real too and is available only on the User object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: An administrator created a record trigger flow to update contacts. How should the administrator reference the values of the active record the flow is running on?
optionD: Use the Get Records element to find the Id.
explanation:
In a record-triggered flow the triggering record is already loaded and available as the $Record global variable, so its fields are referenced directly - $Record.Email, $Record.AccountId - with no query of any kind.
Its companion is worth knowing: $Record__Prior holds the values the record had immediately before the save, which is how a flow detects that a particular field changed.
The alternatives are all wrong shapes. There is no {!Contact.Id} global variable. An {!Account.Id} record variable refers to the wrong object entirely. And a Get Records element would spend a query retrieving a record the flow was handed for free - which on a before-save flow also loses the performance advantage that makes those flows worth using.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_resources_global_variables.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator has reviewed an upcoming critical update. How should the administrator proceed with activation of the critical update?
optionA: Activate the critical update in a sandbox.
optionB: Allow the critical update to auto-activate.
optionC: Activate the critical update in production.
optionD: Allow the critical update to auto-activate in a sandbox.
explanation:
The safe sequence is to activate the update in a sandbox first, exercise the customizations and integrations that could be affected, and only then let it take effect in production. That is the whole point of the window Salesforce gives you before auto-activation: it is time to test, not time to wait.
Activating straight into production skips the test. Allowing auto-activation - in production or in a sandbox - surrenders the choice of when to find out what breaks.
One naming note for the current platform: these are now called Release Updates. The Critical Updates node was retired and replaced by Release Updates in Setup, but the guidance is unchanged - test in a sandbox before the enforcement date.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.release_updates.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Dream house realty needs to use consistent picklist values in the category field on accounts and cases, with values respective to record types. Choose 2 options
explanation:
The consistency half of this requirement is clear. A global value set is one list of values maintained in one place and shared by picklist fields on more than one object, so the Category field on Account and the Category field on Case draw from the same values and stay in step.
The record type half is where this item is weak, and it is worth knowing why. Making values "respective to record types" is done by record types themselves: Edit Picklists for Record Types and Business Processes describes selecting a record type and editing the picklist field to change which values it offers. A dependent picklist does something different - it filters one picklist by the value chosen in a controlling picklist on the same record, which has nothing to do with record types.
The key is left as the source had it, but treat the second half as unreliable. The mechanism that actually varies values by record type is record-type picklist assignment on the custom picklist field, not a dependent picklist.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.editing_picklists_for_record_types_and_business_processes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_recordtype_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

corrected.note: The item pairs a global value set, which is right for consistency across objects, with a dependent picklist, which does not vary values by record type - record-type picklist assignment does. The key is unchanged because the documentation does not settle which option the source intended as the second answer, but the dependent-picklist half does not support the stem.

question: A user at Cloud Kicks is having issues logging in to Salesforce. The user asks the administrator to reset their password. Which two options should the administrator consider when resetting the user's password? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Resetting the password will change the user's password policy.
optionB: Single sign-on users can reset their own passwords using the forgot password link.
optionC: Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocks the user's account.
optionD: After resetting a password, the user may be required to activate their device to successfully log in to Salesforce.
explanation:
Reset Passwords for Your Users lists the considerations, and two of them are these options word for word.
"Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocks the user's account" - so an admin dealing with a lockout does not have to click Unlock separately; the reset covers it.
"After an admin resets a password, users are sometimes required to activate their devices to successfully log in to Salesforce" - identity verification treats the next login as coming from an unrecognised device and asks the user to confirm it.
The same article rules out the option about single sign-on: only an admin can reset SSO user passwords, so those users cannot help themselves through the forgot password link. And a password reset changes one user's password; it does not alter the password policy, which is org-level or profile-level configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.resetting_and_expiring_passwords.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_unlock.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The explanation on this question was about the page layout editor - text belonging to a different item entirely - and never addressed password resets. It has been replaced with the documented considerations, which confirm the existing key.

question: Support agent at Cloud Kicks are spending too much time finding resources to solve cases. The agents need a more efficient way to find documentation and similar cases from the Case page layout. How should an administrator meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a custom object to capture popular case resolutions.
optionB: Use an interview flow to capture Case details.
optionC: Direct users to Global Search to look for similar cases.
optionD: Configure Knowledge with articles and data categories.
explanation:
Knowledge is the feature built for this. Articles hold the documented solutions, and data categories classify them, which does two jobs at once: it organises the knowledge base and it controls who may see which articles.
The payoff on the Case page is suggested articles. Case fields can be mapped to data categories, so when a case is saved Salesforce searches for articles sharing its keywords and floats the ones matching the case's category to the top of the list - agents get candidate solutions without leaving the case.
A custom object to hold popular resolutions rebuilds a weaker version of Knowledge with no article lifecycle, no categorisation and no suggestion engine. An interview flow collects details rather than surfacing answers. Sending agents to global search is what they are already doing too slowly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.knowledge_whatis.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.category_whatis.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The sales team at Ursa Major Solar has asked the administrator to automate an outbound message. What should the administrator utilize to satisfy the request?
explanation:
An outbound message is configured in Setup and then fired by an automation, and Salesforce documents flows as one of the things it can be associated with: outbound messages can be associated with flows, workflow rules, approval processes, or entitlement processes. A record-triggered flow that runs after the record is saved is therefore the current way to automate one.
Process Builder is the distractor to be careful about. It could invoke an outbound message historically, but Salesforce has retired it in favour of Flow, so it is not what an administrator should be told to build today. A case auto-response rule sends an email reply to an inbound case and has nothing to do with a SOAP message to an external endpoint, and task assignment creates work for a user inside Salesforce.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.workflow_managing_outbound_messages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Administrator at Cloud Kicks need to automatically route support cases, regardless of how they are created, to a queue based on case priority. What tool should the administrator use?
explanation:
Assignment rules are the routing engine for cases, and the phrase that matters in this stem is "regardless of how they are created". An active case assignment rule runs on cases arriving from Web-to-Case, Email-to-Case, the API and On-Demand Email-to-Case, as well as ones created in the UI when the rule is applied - so one rule covers every channel.
Each rule holds ordered entries; an entry that tests Priority sends matching cases to the queue for that priority, and the first matching entry wins.
Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case are channels rather than routing tools - they create cases, they do not decide who works them. Auto-response rules reply to the customer and change no ownership at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.creating_assignment_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.customize_leadrules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) needs a new sales application. The administrator there is an application package on the AppExchange and wants to begin testing it in a sandbox to see If it addresses CK's needs. What are two considerations when installing a managed package in a sandbox? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Any metadata changes to the package have to be recreated in production.
optionB: The installation link has to be modified to test.saiesiorcc.com.
optionC: Install for Admins Only will be the only Install option available.
optionD: The package will be removed any time the sandbox is refreshed.
explanation:
A package's install URL points at login.salesforce.com, which resolves to production, so to install into a sandbox the administrator replaces login with test in that URL. And because refreshing a sandbox rebuilds it from its source org, a package installed only in the sandbox disappears at the next refresh unless the source org carries it too.
Install for Admins Only is one of three install options — alongside Install for All Users and Install for Specific Profiles — not the only one available. Metadata changes made inside a sandbox do have to be reproduced in production, but that is true of any sandbox work and is not specific to installing a managed package.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The explanation names the modified test.salesforce.com install link and the loss of the package on sandbox refresh — B and D. The answer key had C, which is simply false: Install for Admins Only is one of several install options, not the only one.

question: An administrator at Universal Containers needs a simple way to trigger an alert to the director of sales when opportunities reach an amount of $500,000. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?
optionA: Set up Big Deal Alerts for the amount.
optionD: Key Deals component on the homepage
explanation:
A Big Deal Alert is a standard setting that emails people when an opportunity crosses a threshold, which is exactly the "simple way" the stem asks for - no automation to build and no code.
One detail to carry into the exam: the threshold is a pair, not a single number. Set Up Big Deal Alerts for Opportunities has you enter both a trigger amount in the corporate currency and a trigger probability, and the alert fires when an opportunity reaches both. It fires once; if the amount or probability later fall below the threshold and climb back, it fires again.
Opportunity update reminders are scheduled nudges to owners about stale records. Kanban alerts flag deals needing attention inside that view only. There is no Key Deals home page component.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.activating_big_deal_alerts.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is creating a validation rule. Which two functions should the administrator use when creating a validation rule? Choose 2 answers
explanation:
Defining a validation rule comes down to two things you must supply.
The error condition formula is the test. It is written so that a result of TRUE means the record is invalid - which trips people up, because the formula describes the condition you want to block, not the one you want to allow.
The error message location decides where the message appears: at the top of the page, or attached to a specific field so the user is pointed straight at what to fix.
Neither of the other two exists here. A formula return type is something you choose when creating a formula field; a validation rule's result is always a Boolean. And there is no active date on a validation rule - it is simply active or inactive.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Aw Computing needs to capture a loss reason in rich text field when an opportunity is Closed lost. How should an administrator configure this requirement?
optionA: Select the requirement checkbox next to the loss reason field on the page layout.
optionB: Create a validation rule to display an error if stage is Closed lost and Loss Reason is blank.
optionC: Check the required checkbox on the Loss Reason field in Object Manger.
optionD: Configure a workflow rule to display an error if Loss Reason is blank
explanation:
The requirement is conditional - Loss Reason is needed only when the Stage is Closed Lost - and that is precisely what a validation rule expresses and nothing else here can.
The rule tests for the combination and blocks the save with a message: stage equals Closed Lost and Loss Reason is blank.
Both of the "required" options fail because required is unconditional. Marking the field required on the page layout, or required in Object Manager, would demand a loss reason on every opportunity from the moment it is created, including ones that go on to be won. The Object Manager setting is the stricter of the two, applying to the API as well as the UI.
A workflow rule cannot display an error or stop a save at all; it acts after the record is saved.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to track shoe designs by products. Shoe designs should be unable to be deleted, and there can be multiple designs for one product across various stages. Which two steps should the administrator configure to meet this requirement? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Add a custom master-detail field for shoe designs on the Product object,
optionB: Create a custom object for shoe designs.
optionC: Use the standard object for designs.
optionD: Configure a custom lookup field for shoe designs on the Product object.
explanation:
There is no standard object for shoe designs, so the first step is a custom object.
The second step is the relationship, and the constraint decides it. Master-detail would cascade: delete a Product and every design under it is deleted too, which is the opposite of designs that cannot be deleted. A lookup on the Product side leaves each design standing on its own, while still allowing many designs to point at one product and to sit at different stages.
Protecting the designs from deletion is then a permissions question - withhold Delete on the object - rather than a relationship question.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
_cat: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: The administrator at AW Computing wants to send off client welcome tasks and a welcome email to the primary contact automatically when an Opportunity is Closed won. What automation tool best accomplishes this?
explanation:
Of the four options, only one is an automation tool that can create a task and send an email off the back of a record change, and that is Process Builder. A validation rule can only block a save. An outbound message sends record data to an external endpoint. An approval process routes a record for sign-off.
The exam answer stands, but build it in Flow. Salesforce ended support for Workflow Rules and Process Builder on 31 December 2025; existing automation still runs and can still be edited, but new work belongs in a record-triggered flow, which does both halves of this requirement - a Create Records element for the welcome task and an email action to the primary contact.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator has assigned a permission set group with the two-factor authentication for User Interface Logins permissions and the two-factor authentication for API Logins permission to a group of users. Which two prompts will happen when one of the users attempts to log in to Data Loader? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Users need to connect an authenticator app to their Salesforce account.
optionB: Users need to get a security token from a trusted network using Reset My Security Token.
optionC: Users need to download and install an authenticator app on theirmobile device.
optionD: Users need to enter a verification code from email or SMS, whichever has higher priority.
explanation:
Requiring multi-factor authentication for API logins means the Data Loader sign-in now needs a verification code, and a user who has no registered method is walked through enrolling one on that first attempt. That is the two prompts: install a TOTP authenticator app on a mobile device, then connect it to the Salesforce account by scanning the QR code or pasting the security key shown during enrolment.
Codes delivered by email or SMS are not accepted as Salesforce MFA verification methods, so no such prompt appears. A security token is a separate mechanism appended to the password for API access — it is emailed when reset rather than requested at login, so it is not one of the prompts either.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.security_require_2fa_api.htm&type=5

corrected.note: Email and SMS codes are not valid Salesforce MFA verification methods, so the previously marked option cannot describe a real prompt. Enrolling a TOTP app is a two-step sequence — install the app, then connect it to the account — which is what the user is actually asked for.

question: Northern Trail Outfitters is using one profile for all of its marketing users, providing read-only access to the Campaign object. A few marketing users now require comprehensive edit access on Campaigns. How should an administrator fulfil this request?
explanation:
A permission set grants extra access on top of whatever profile a user already has, which is exactly the shape of this problem: most marketing users should keep read-only access to Campaigns, and a few need edit.
So the administrator builds one permission set with the campaign object permissions and assigns it to those few. Nobody's profile changes and no second marketing profile has to be created and then maintained in parallel.
Organization-wide defaults move the baseline for everyone, not for a few. The Marketing User checkbox is a different control - it governs campaign management features such as creating campaigns and managing members - and it would not grant object edit access on its own. Field-level security governs individual fields, not the ability to edit the record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.perm_sets_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_object_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud kicks want to give credit to Opportunity team members based on the level of effort contributed by each person toward each deal. What feature should the administrator use to meet this requirement?
explanation:
Opportunity splits are the feature for dividing credit on a deal among the opportunity team. Each team member gets a share, and those shares roll into quota and pipeline reporting so the contribution is visible rather than anecdotal.
There are two flavours worth telling apart. Revenue splits divide the amount and must total 100 percent. Overlay splits credit people who helped without owning the revenue - a sales engineer, for example - and are not constrained to total 100 percent.
Stages describe where a deal is, queues hold records awaiting an owner, and list views only filter what you see. None of them allocates credit.
References:

question: Northern Trail Outfitters has requested that when the Referral Date field is updated on the custom object Referral Source, the parent object Referral also needs to be updated. Which automation solution should an administrator use to meet this request?
explanation:
Updating a field on a parent record when a child changes needs an automation tool that can traverse the relationship and write to the related record. Of the options, only Process Builder does that.
A workflow field update cannot: workflow can update a field on the record that triggered it, and on the master of a master-detail relationship, but not on an arbitrary parent. An approval process routes records for sign-off. A Lightning web component is UI code, not automation, and would only act when someone opened the page.
As with the rest of this deck's Process Builder items, the exam answer stands but the modern build is a record-triggered flow on Referral Source with an Update Records element pointed at the parent - Salesforce ended support for Process Builder on 31 December 2025.

question: Northern Trail outfitters has hired interns to enter Leads into Salesforce and has requested a way to is identify these new records from existing Leads. What approach should an administrator take to meet this requirement?
optionA: Set up Web-to-Lead form the interns use.
optionB: Define a record type and assign it to the interns.
optionC: Create a separate Lead Lightning App.
optionD: Update the active Leas Assignment Rules.
explanation:
A record type stamps each record with which process created it, and it is visible, filterable and reportable - so leads entered by the interns can be told apart from the rest simply by their record type, without inventing a custom field for the purpose.
Assigning that record type to the interns' profile (or via a permission set) means it is the one they get, while everyone else keeps the original.
Web-to-Lead creates leads from a form on a website, which is not what interns keying records into Salesforce are doing. A separate Lightning app changes navigation, not the data. Assignment rules decide who owns a lead once it exists; ownership is a poor proxy for who created it, since leads get reassigned.

question: An administrator is building a Lightning app and sees a message that a My Domain must be set up first. What should the administrator take into consideration when enabling My Domain?
optionA: Single sign-on must be disabled prior toimplementing My Domain.
optionB: The login for all internal and external users changes to the My Domain login
optionC: A deployed My Domain is irreversible and renaming is unavailable.
optionD: The URL instance for a My Domain stays the same for every release
explanation:
My Domain replaces the org's instance URL with a branded one, and the consequence users feel immediately is the login URL: everyone signs in at the My Domain address instead of the generic login page. That applies to internal users and to external users on Experience Cloud sites alike.
The other three statements are wrong. Single sign-on does not have to be disabled - the opposite is true, since My Domain is a prerequisite for several SSO and Lightning features. A deployed My Domain is not irreversible: the name can be changed, and Salesforce documents how to manage redirections from the previous host name when you do. And the instance behind an org can move between releases, which is one of the reasons to stop relying on instance URLs in the first place.

question: An administrator at Ursa Major Solar needs to send information to an external accounting system What workflow action should the administrator use to accomplish this?
explanation:
An outbound message is the workflow action built for sending data out of Salesforce. You define which fields to send and the endpoint URL to send them to, and Salesforce posts a SOAP message to that endpoint when the automation fires - which is exactly what handing information to an external accounting system means.
It is declarative, so no Apex is involved, and Salesforce documents it as available to flows, workflow rules, approval processes and entitlement processes.
The alternatives all stay inside Salesforce. Assigning a task creates a record for a user. Create Record does the same for any object. A custom notification pushes an in-app or mobile alert to Salesforce users.
One currency note: since February 2026 outbound messages no longer carry a session id, so the receiving system authenticates with OAuth 2.0 rather than replaying a session from the payload.

question: The sales manager at Cloud Kicks wants to set up a business process where opportunity discounts over 30% need to be approved by the VP of sales. Any discounts above 10% need to be approved by the user's manager. The administrator has been tasked with creating an approval process. Which are two considerations the administrator needs to review before setting up this approval process? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Create a custom Discount field on the opportunity to capture the discount amount
optionB: Populate the Manager standard field on the sales users' User Detail page.
optionD: Allow the submitter choose the approver manually.
explanation:
Both are prerequisites that must be in place before the process can be built. Discount is not a standard field on Opportunity, so a custom field has to exist to hold the percentage that the entry criteria and steps will test. And routing a step to "the user's manager" uses the Manager field on the submitter's user record — if that field is empty the approval has nowhere to go. Salesforce's own Build a Discount Approval Process walkthrough sets up both before creating the process.
Two separate approval processes are not required: a single process with conditional steps covers both tiers, routing anything over 10% to the manager and escalating over 30% to the VP. Letting the submitter choose the approver by hand would defeat the point of routing by discount size.
References:
https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/projects/build-a-discount-approval-process/prepare-your-org

corrected.note: Routing to "the user's manager" only works if the Manager field on the user record is populated, which makes it a genuine prerequisite. Two separate approval processes are not one: a single process with conditional steps handles both the 10% and 30% tiers.

question: Cloud Kicks want its reports to show a Fiscal Year that starts on February 1 and has 12 months. How Should the Administrator Address this requirement?
optionA: Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the starting month as February.
optionB: Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the duration to 4 quarters.
optionC: Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the starting month as February.
optionD: Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the duration to 12 months.
explanation:
Standard fiscal years in Salesforce follow the Gregorian calendar but may begin on the first day of any month, so a twelve-month year beginning 1 February is precisely a standard fiscal year with February chosen as the starting month.
Custom fiscal years exist for structures that do not map onto calendar months at all — 4-4-5 period layouts, 13-period years, or quarters built from a set number of weeks. Choosing Custom here would mean defining every period by hand to reproduce what the standard setting already provides, and once a custom fiscal year is enabled the feature cannot be turned back off.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.setting_the_fiscal_year.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: A standard fiscal year in Salesforce may begin on the first day of ANY month, so a 12-month year starting 1 February is exactly a standard fiscal year. Custom fiscal years exist for structures that do not follow calendar months (4-4-5, 13 periods). The explanation's claim that a standard year must start on January 1 is wrong.

question: AW Computing would like to improve its Case Lightning record page by including: * A filtered component to display a message in bold font when a case is saved as acriticalrecord type. * A quick way to update the account status from the case layout. Which two components should an administrator use to satisfy these requests? Choose 2 Answers
explanation:
Two requests, two standard Lightning page components.
The Related Record component surfaces a related record's fields on this page and allows them to be edited in place - so an agent can update the account's status without leaving the case. It needs an update action to define which fields are editable.
The Rich Text component holds formatted text, which is what makes the bold message possible. Pair it with a component visibility filter on record type so it appears only on critical cases.
A Related List shows child records rather than editable parent fields. The Record Detail component shows the case's own fields, not the account's.

question: Ursa Major Solar provides a 1-year warranty on all of the panels it installs. Installation details, along with the warranty information, a captured on a custom object called Installation. The installation record is created by the installer from the mobile app. Customers son receive a longer warranty as a way of increasing customer satisfaction when an installation gets delayed or has issues. How should the administrator configure Salesforce to capture the expiration date of the warranty?
optionA: Use a formula as the default value of the warranty Expiration Date field.
optionB: Create a formula field to display l year from the warranty purchased.
optionC: Add a validation rule to ensure the Expiration Date field is populated.
optionD: Include the warranty Expiration Date field on the mobile page layout.
explanation:
The requirement has two halves that pull in opposite directions: the date should normally be a year after installation, but it must be possible to give a customer a longer warranty. A default value formula does both - it calculates the usual date when the record is created, and leaves the field writable so anyone can override it afterwards.
A formula field cannot be overridden at all. It recalculates from its inputs every time it is read, so a goodwill extension would be impossible to record.
A validation rule only insists that the field is filled in; it never works out what the value should be. Adding the field to the mobile layout makes it visible to the installer but supplies no date, which just moves the typing onto the person in the field.

explanation:

question: Users at Cloud Kicks want to be able to create a task that will repeat every two weeks. What should an administrator do to meet the requirement?
optionC: Workflow rule to create recurring tasks.
explanation:
Recurring tasks are switched on at org level, not per user. Enable Recurring Tasks in Lightning Experience and the Salesforce Mobile App gives the path: from Setup, find Activity Settings, select Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks, and save. After that, add the Create Recurring Series of Tasks field to the task page layouts so users can actually set a recurrence - here, every two weeks.
No automation is needed. A flow or a workflow rule could manufacture a series of separate task records, but they would be unrelated tasks rather than a recurring series, with no series to view or delete as a unit.
There is no setting called Turn on Recurring Activities.

question: The business development team at Cloud Kicks thinks the account creation process has too many fields to fill out and the page feels cluttered. They have requested the administrator to simplify the process. Which automation tool should an administrator use?
explanation:
The complaint is about the shape of the data-entry experience, and a screen flow is the only tool here that can change it. Flow Builder can present a short, ordered sequence of screens asking for just the fields that matter, branch on what the user answers, and create the account at the end - so the clutter of a full page layout never appears.
The other three do not build user interfaces. An approval process routes a record for sign-off after it exists. A workflow rule acts after a save and cannot collect input. A validation rule can only reject a save, which makes data entry more frustrating rather than less.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.create_forms_with_screen_flow_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks users are seeing error messages when they use one of their screen flows. The error messages are confusing but could be resolved if the users entered more information on the account before starting the flow. How should the administrator address this issues?
optionA: Remove validation rules so that the users are able to process without complete records.
optionB: Create a permission set to allow users to bypass the error.
optionC: use a fault connector and display a screen with text explaining what went wrong and how to correct it.
optionD: Uncheck the end user Flow Errors box in setup.
explanation:
The users are not hitting a bug - they are hitting a real failure with an unhelpful message. A fault connector is how a flow catches that. Drag the fault path off the element that fails and route it to a screen whose display text explains, in the org's own words, what is missing and how to fix it.
That leaves the underlying rules intact, which matters because the alternatives all work by removing protection. Deleting the validation rules lets incomplete accounts save. A permission set that bypasses the error does the same for a subset of users. Suppressing flow error emails hides the problem from the administrator without changing anything the user sees.
References:

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.create_forms_with_screen_flow_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The administrator at cloud kicks is trying to debug a screen flow that create contacts. One of the variables in the flow is missing on the debug screen. What could cause this issue?
optionA: The available for input checkbox was unchecked.
optionB: The flow is an inactive version
optionC: The field type is unsupported by debugging.
optionD: The available for output checkbox was unchecked.
explanation:
The debug window offers a value for a variable only when that variable can be set from outside the flow, and that is what Available for input controls. Clear the checkbox and the variable still exists and still works inside the flow - it simply stops accepting a value from a caller, a URL parameter, or the debug screen, so it disappears from the list of inputs.
Available for output is the mirror image: it governs whether the value can be read by whatever called the flow, and has no effect on what debug asks for.
The other two explain nothing. Debugging runs against a specific version rather than requiring an active one, and there is no field type that debug refuses to show.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator has been asked to update a flow that was created as part of a recent update. When the administrator opens the flow for editing, the Flow toolbox offers only four elements: Assignment, Decision, Get Records, and Loop. What would cause this?
optionA: The flow is a screen flow.
optionB: The version of the flow is inactive.
optionC: The flow is a before save flow.
optionD: The version of the flow is activated.
explanation:
A before-save record-triggered flow runs inside the save itself, before the record is written, and that is why its toolbox is so short: Assignment, Decision, Get Records, and Loop. It can read data and work out values, then set fields on the triggering record through $Record - but it cannot create, update or delete anything, call an action, or show a screen.
That restriction is the price of the speed. Because the flow writes to the record already in memory, there is no second save, which is what makes before-save flows dramatically faster than the after-save equivalent for same-record field updates.
An after-save flow gets the full element set. A screen flow is not record-triggered at all. Whether a version is active or inactive changes nothing about which elements are offered.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_ref_elements.htm&type=5

question: When a cloud kicks Opportunity closes, the company would like to automatically create a renewal opportunity. Which automation tool should an administrator use to accomplish this request?
explanation:
Creating a renewal opportunity means inserting a record, and Flow Builder is the only tool offered here that can do that: a record-triggered flow fires when the opportunity closes, and a Create Records element builds the renewal from the closing deal.
A validation rule only blocks a save when a condition fails — it can never create anything. An approval process routes an existing record for sign-off, and a sharing rule governs who can see a record, neither of which produces a new opportunity.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.flow_considerations_trigger_record.htm&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks needs to change the owner of a case when it has been open for more than 7 days. How should the administrator complete this requirement?
explanation:
Only one tool here measures elapsed time. An escalation rule entry ages a case from its creation date, and when the case passes the threshold - seven days in this scenario - its escalation actions run. Reassigning the case to another user or a queue is one of the two things those actions can do; sending notification email is the other.
Assignment rules fire when a case is created or reassigned, so they cannot notice that a week has gone by. Auto-response rules reply to the customer and change nothing about ownership. A validation rule can only block a save.
One configuration detail that trips people up: escalation ages are counted against business hours, so a rule intended to fire after seven calendar days needs business hours that run around the clock.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_supporthours.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which three items are available in the mobile navigation menu? Choose 3 answers
explanation:
The mobile navigation menu is built from things that behave like tabs. Anything represented by a tab is eligible - standard and custom objects, the Chatter feed, People and Groups - and to that Salesforce adds Lightning app pages, Visualforce pages and a set of productivity items, Dashboards among them. What each user actually sees is still filtered by their profile's tab settings.
So Lightning app pages, Chatter and Dashboards are all menu items. The Lightning Home page is not: it is the landing page of a Lightning app rather than an entry in the menu. Nor is the utility bar, which is a docked strip along the bottom of a desktop Lightning app and does not exist in the mobile app at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.salesforce_app_customize_nav_menu.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has two sales teams, Sales team A and Sales team B. Each team has their own role in the role hierarchy. Both roles are subordinates of the same Manager role. How Should the administrator share records owned by sales team A with Sales team B?
explanation:
An owner-based sharing rule shares records according to who owns them: set it to share the records owned by the Sales Team A role with the Sales Team B role, and every current and future record follows automatically.
Manual sharing grants access one record at a time and is performed by the record owner, so it neither scales to a whole team nor is something an administrator configures centrally. The role hierarchy only grants access upward, which is why the shared Manager role can see both teams' records while the two peer roles still cannot see each other's. Criteria-based sharing keys off field values on the record rather than off its owner, so it does not express "owned by Sales Team A".
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Sharing the records owned by one role with another peer role is the textbook use of an owner-based sharing rule. Manual sharing is a per-record action taken by the owner, not something an administrator configures for a whole team.

question: Which tool should an administrator use to identify and fix potential session vulnerabilities?
explanation:
Health Check is the page built for this. It reads the org's security settings, compares them against a baseline - the Salesforce Baseline Standard, or one of up to five custom baselines you upload - and reports a score with the settings that fall short grouped as High, Medium, Low risk or Informational. Session settings are among the settings it grades.
The part that answers "and fix" is Fix Risks, which resets the flagged settings to the baseline's recommended values without leaving the page.
The alternatives report on other things: Setup Audit Trail lists configuration changes, Field History Tracking records changes to record data, and organization-wide defaults are one of the settings Health Check grades rather than a tool for finding weak ones.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_health_check.htm&language=en_US&type=5

The two that matter for the Salesforce mobile app are the App page — a custom page of components that appears as an item in the mobile navigation menu — and the Record page, which lays out an individual record for viewing and editing.
There is no User page or Dashboard page type in App Builder. Dashboards are built in the Reports and Dashboards tools and can only be surfaced on a Lightning page as a component.

question: What is the order of execution when a Case record is saved?
optionA: Validation rules, Escalation rules, Workflow rules, Auto-response rules
optionB: Assignment rules, Auto-response rules, Workflow rules, Escalation rules
optionC: Assignment rules, Validation rules, Workflow rules, Escalation rules
optionD: Validation rules, Assignment rules, Escalation rules, Auto-response rules
explanation:
The Apex Developer Guide sets out the save order, and for a Case the four rules in these options run in this sequence: after triggers, then assignment rules, then auto-response rules, then workflow rules, and — after the workflow field updates and their re-validation — escalation rules.
That ordering is what rules out the alternatives. Validation runs well before any of the four (it is part of the system validation steps that precede the save), so any sequence opening with validation rules and placing assignment or escalation after it misdescribes the save. Escalation rules run last of the four, not second or third: an escalation is evaluated after the record has been written and after workflow has had its turn.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm

question: The administrator has been asked to automate a simple field update on the account. When a support agent changes the status of the account to 'Audited', they would like the system to automatically update the Audited date field on the account with today's date. Which tool should the administrator use to complete this automation?
explanation:
Recording the date a status changed means writing a value into the Audited Date field, and a record-triggered flow on Account does exactly that: when Status becomes "Audited", an Update Records element stamps the date into the field, where it then stays.
A formula field fails here for two separate reasons. It is read-only and computes a value for display rather than storing one, so it cannot populate a different field. And a formula returning TODAY() re-evaluates every day, so it would always show the current date rather than the day the account was audited.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: A formula field is read-only and cannot write a value into another field. It would also give the wrong result: TODAY() re-evaluates every day, so the stamp would drift instead of recording when the status changed. Writing a date on a field change needs Flow Builder.

question: Universal Containers administrator has been asked to create a many-to-many relationship between two existing custom objects. Which two steps should the administrator take when enabling the many-to-many relationship? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Create a junction with a custom object.
optionB: Create two master detail relationships on the new object.
optionC: Create two lookup relationships on the new object.
optionD: Create URL fields on a custom object.
explanation:
Salesforce has no many-to-many relationship type, so you build one out of parts. Create a custom object to sit between the two - the junction object - and give it two master-detail relationships, one to each side.
The order matters in practice: the first master-detail you create becomes the primary relationship, which determines the junction record's look and feel, its owner, and which parent's sharing it inherits.
Two lookups would technically link the objects but would give up what master-detail provides here - required parents, so no junction record can be orphaned, cascade delete when a parent goes, and roll-up summaries on either side. URL fields link to addresses and create no relationship at all.

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has deployed my domain. The Chief Marketing Officer wants to make sure that all of the Salesforce users log in using the branded login URL. There needs to be a grace period for the user's bookmarks to be updated. How should the administrator configure the policies in my domain settings?
optionA: Set the login policy to require login from https://nto.my.salesforce.com
optionB: Set the Redirect policy to Do Not redirect.
optionC: Set the redirect policy to Redirect with a warning to the same page within the domain.
optionD: Set the login policy to prevent login from https://login.salesforce.com
explanation:
The requirement contains its own answer: users must end up on the branded URL, but there has to be a grace period while bookmarks are updated. Redirecting with a warning does both - the user still arrives where they were going, and sees a message telling them the address has changed.
Not redirecting at all leaves the old URLs working silently, so nobody ever updates a bookmark. The two login-policy options are the opposite of a grace period: blocking logins from the generic login page cuts off anyone still using an old bookmark immediately, which is the right end state but the wrong first step.
The usual sequence is therefore to redirect with a warning first, and tighten the login policy once traffic on the old URLs has died away.

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) stores information about specific customers in Contacts and information about shoes and accessories in a custom Merchandise object. What should the CK administrator use to represent that Contact can be interested in multiple pieces of Merchandies?
explanation:
A junction object is a type of custom object that allows administrators to create many-to-many relationships between two other objects. A many-to-many relationship means that each record of one object can be related to multiple records of another object, and vice versa. For example, a junction object can represent that a contact can be interested in multiple pieces of merchandise, and a piece of merchandise can be of interest to multiple contacts. A junction object has two master-detail relationships with the two objects it connects.

question: An administrator installed a managed package that contains a permission set group. The permission set group that was installed includes Delete access on several objects, and the administrator needs to prevent users in the permission set group from being able to delete records. What should the administrator do to control Delete access?
optionA: Use a muting permission set with a permission set group to mute selected permissions.
optionB: Create a new permission set that has Delete access deselected for the objects.
optionC: Create a new role that prevents Delete permissions from rolling up to the users.
optionD: Edit the profile for the users to remove Delete access from the objects.
explanation:
The permission set group came from a managed package, so its permission sets cannot be edited. A muting permission set is the mechanism designed for exactly that: it sits inside the group and disables selected permissions the group would otherwise grant, without touching the packaged permission sets themselves.
So the administrator adds a muting permission set to the group and mutes Delete on the objects concerned. Users assigned to that group lose Delete; anyone assigned one of those permission sets directly, outside the group, is unaffected.
A new permission set cannot help - permissions are additive, and deselecting an access in one permission set never takes away what another grants. Editing the profile fails for the same reason, since the group grants Delete regardless of the profile. Roles govern record visibility, not object permissions.

question: An administration needs to store the ID of record type of later use in a flow. Which kind of variable should the administrator use?
explanation:
Flow variable data types are Text, Number, Currency, Boolean, Date, Date/Time, Picklist, Multi-Select Picklist, Record and Apex-Defined. There is no ID type, so a record type id — an 18-character string — is held in a Text variable.
A Record variable stores a whole record and its fields rather than a single id value, and a Boolean holds only true or false.

question: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is unable to add a new user in salesforce. What could cause this issue?
optionA: The Username is not a corporate email address
optionB: The username is less than 80 characters.
optionC: The Username is a fake email address.
optionD: The Username is already in use.
explanation:
A Salesforce username has to be unique across every Salesforce org in existence - production, sandbox and trial alike - so the usual reason a new user will not save is that the username has already been taken somewhere.
The format rules explain why the other options are wrong. A username must look like an email address, but it does not have to be a working one and it does not have to belong to the company's domain, so neither a non-corporate nor a fictitious address blocks the save. The length limit is 80 characters as a maximum, so being under 80 is a requirement met rather than a problem.
The practical workaround is to keep the person's real email in the Email field and give the username a suffix that makes it globally unique.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.users_adding_guidelines.htm&language=en_US&type=5
